lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: applications and interviews

objective: Learners complete a short fictional job application for a made-up part-time role, listing only name, interests, and availability, then rehearse answering and asking interview questions out loud with a willing adult or peer playing a fictional hiring manager, practicing both content and delivery under low-stakes conditions.
scenario: The fictional Cedar Lane Smoothie Bar is hiring a part-time crew member. The learner fills out a short application listing only their name, interests, and realistic availability, then sits down with an available adult or peer who reads from a short interviewer script as Jordan Whitfield, the fictional hiring manager, while the learner answers three questions out loud and asks one question back.
safetyNotes: The mock interview is private practice within the household with a willing, available adult or peer, never a real employer, and is never performed publicly or recorded.
Cedar Lane Smoothie Bar and Jordan Whitfield are entirely fictional; no real application is submitted anywhere.

simulationAlternative.description: If no partner is available for a live practice interview, write out both a set of five interview questions and your own answers to each instead.

materials: the fictional job posting on this task sheet
the interviewer script on this task sheet

tasks.directions: Read the fictional Cedar Lane Smoothie Bar job posting on this task sheet before filling out anything.

prompts.text: Name two things about this fictional role that connect to your own real interests or past responsibilities.

tasks.directions: Fill out the short fictional application: your first name, two or three genuine interests, and realistic weekly availability. Do not write a real address, real ID number, or any information beyond what is asked for.

prompts.text: My application lists only my first name, interests, and availability, with no address, phone number, or ID number of any kind.
Write the availability section of your application: which days and roughly which hours you'd realistically be free for a fictional part-time shift.

tasks.directions: With an available adult or peer playing Jordan Whitfield, the fictional hiring manager, sit across from your partner and answer three interview questions out loud: why are you interested in this role, describe a time you finished something on a deadline, and how would you handle being asked to do a task you were not trained for yet. After answering, ask your partner one question back about the fictional role, such as what a typical shift looks like.

prompts.text: Summarize, in your own words, how you answered the deadline question during the live interview and what specific question you asked Jordan Whitfield back at the end.

tasks.directions: Think back on how the live interview actually went.

prompts.text: Which of the three questions was hardest to answer out loud, and what would you change about your answer if you could redo it?

remediation: If a learner's spoken answers stay one word or trail off ('I don't know, just because'), reteach by writing one full answer together first using a simple pattern (name the example, what you did, what happened), then have the learner practice saying that written answer out loud twice before attempting a new question unscripted.
extension: Have the learner write two follow-up questions Jordan Whitfield might realistically ask after their answers, and practice responding to those on the spot with their partner.
